notes: The discontinuous 'for … sake' wrap heads on 'for', its carrier being the proper preposition διά (rule 78); rule 46's postpositional χάριν case does not arise.
ἃ → 'which things' heads on the generic noun (rule 77), which is the contrast to rule 17's demonstrative and quantifier cases elsewhere in the chapter.
Both genitive article–noun pairs decided the same way: no English determiner, so the article is unrepresented and the case preposition rides with the noun (rules 21, 23, 24).
